subject: F-Droid recipe validation and release-build reproduction
toolchain: Ubuntu OpenJDK 21.0.13.0.3, Gradle 8.11.1 (wrapper), Android SDK 35, Build Tools 35.0.0, AGP 8.9.2

recipeChecks.rewritemeta: no changes (recipe already in canonical form)
recipeChecks.scanner: wrapper removals only (gradlew, gradlew.bat, gradle-wrapper.jar) at v1.0, v1.0.1, v1.0.1.1, v1.0.1.2; no warnings, no errors
recipeChecks.checkupdates: from CurrentVersion 1.0.1.1 / CurrentVersionCode 3 it updated to 1.0.1.2 (4), reading versionCode from app/build.gradle.kts at the tags

releaseBuilds.command: ./gradlew --no-daemon :app:assembleRelease (twice on machine A), then assembleRelease from app/ (machine A, the subdir fdroidserver uses), then twice on machine B with build outputs deleted between runs

projectChecks.tools/check_release.py: pass on the rebuilt unsigned APK

publishedComparison.explanation: tools/package_release.py re-zips the APK before aligning and signing it, so Python zlib re-deflates 16 entries. Replaying that filter plus zipalign -P 16 reproduced the published compressed size and CRC for all 270 entries.
publishedComparison.apksigcopier: 1.1.1 with apksigner 0.9: DOES NOT VERIFY (APK Signature Scheme v3, CHUNKED_SHA256 digest mismatch), because the chunked digest covers the recompressed entries. Upstream-signature reproduction is therefore not claimed; the recipe sets no Binaries and no AllowedAPKSigningKeys.

secondMachine.detail: A second cloud machine installed the Android SDK from Google's commandlinetools archive during the run and built the same tag twice; both builds match the reference hash and size exactly, and cmp reports the files byte-identical.
secondMachine.sharedInputs: Repository contents, the Gradle wrapper and its pinned checksum, and public Maven artifacts; the SDK was downloaded independently on each machine.
secondMachine.unverified: F-Droid's buildserver: it uses Debian-packaged JDK and build tools and replaces the Gradle wrapper, and no F-Droid build has been compared to these bytes. Nothing was exercised on hardware.
